steps.label: after the answers to the questions

items.note: Matches ESC 2021 diuretic flowchart (urine Na at 2 h, output at 6 h, double the loop dose first); key is the only defensible option; right pitch for acute medicine.
High-gradient severe AS with LVEF 45% and no other cause is a class I indication; distractors each fit a different scenario; one clear best answer.
Key right per ESC 2023 (high, not very high risk). Quibbles: fondaparinux given though angiography <24 h planned (UFH preferred); GRACE 152 looks high, I estimate ~140.
Coherent, realistic thyrotoxic AF; calcium/ALP/PTH, scan and flat troponin fit; key tests on-label DOAC reduction and the 24 h cardioversion rule (ESC 2024, checked).

feedback.note: Grades fair; ACS IIa downgrade and trials accurate; open about what was not re-read. 2025 AS early-intervention IIa put loosely (omits LVEF >=50%, low risk); ESC summary checked.
Ticks fair to a complete answer; ESC 2024 claims checked against a guideline summary; Burch-Wartofsky sums and Nakazawa figures correct and hedged; teaches dose criteria both ways.

quality.note: Accurate, current (ESC 2021-2025), well pitched for internal medicine; grading fair; unverified points flagged. Minor quibbles only: Q3 stem and one loosely worded 2025 valve pearl.
concerns: Q3 stem: fondaparinux before angiography planned within 24 h; ESC 2023 prefers UFH in that setting and fondaparinux when angiography is not expected within 24 h.
Q3 stem: a GRACE score of 152 looks high for the data given (my estimate about 140); it does not change the key, since confirmed NSTEMI is itself a high-risk criterion.
Q2 feedback: the 2025 class IIa for early intervention applies to asymptomatic high-gradient severe AS with LVEF >=50% and low procedural risk, not 'in general'.
Q2 feedback: class I for LVEF <50% in the 2025 text was not re-read by the examiner (it says so); I believe it is retained but did not open the full text either.
Q3 feedback: the stated reason for the IIa downgrade (difficulty reaching a PCI centre in time) is the examiner's inference; I could not confirm it from the guideline.
